intended_object: The canonical projection K_0^{Laurent}(P) → K_0^{Laurent}(P)/rad_L, of ℤ[q,q⁻¹]-modules. Here rad_L is the left radical of the graded Ext-Euler (q-Euler) pairing, the "left numerical Grothendieck group" of Dancso–Licata §3.1. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition unfolds to `leftNumericalQuotientMk b`, which is `(leftRadical b).mkQ`. Here `b` is the graded Ext-Euler sesquilinear pairing and `leftRadical b = b.ker`, i.e. {x | ∀ y, b x y = 0}. The library's own lemma `mem_gradedExtEulerLeftRadical_iff` states exactly this.

The kernel of a semilinear map (semilinear here through `invert`) is a submodule, so the quotient is a ℤ[q,q⁻¹]-module and `mkQ` is the ℤ[q,q⁻¹]-linear quotient map. The codomain `GradedExtEulerLeftNumericalQuotient` is precisely this quotient. So the definition is the standard projection onto the left numerical Grothendieck group.

It specializes the library's generic numerical-quotient construction to one particular pairing. As a named, specific object, that does not make it too narrow. Mathlib has `Submodule.mkQ`, which this definition uses, but no named "numerical quotient" construction.
